title: Fix Storybook Build Broken By Puzzle DSL Fixture Migration
description:
Storybook's production build (bun nx run workspace:build-storybook) fails repo-wide with "Could not resolve" errors, blocking every Playwright spec under .storybook/ since Vite bundles all stories in one pass. Root cause: three story files still import fixture files with old extensions (.2d.json/.3d.json/.5d.json) that ticket 26/07/26/CONVERT-PUZZLE-2D-3D-5D-TO-TYPED-DSL-DERIVE-ENGINE deleted/renamed to .puzzle2d/.puzzle3d/.puzzle5d DSL-text fixtures:
- .storybook/stories/puzzle/2d/Fixtures.stories.tsx
- .storybook/stories/puzzle/3d/World.stories.tsx
- .storybook/stories/puzzle/5d/Timeline.stories.tsx

Research confirmed there is no existing TS-side DSL parser anywhere in the repo, and no existing free (non-stateful) wasm_bindgen export that converts DSL text to JSON. Plan: add one small free #[wasm_bindgen] function per crate (puzzle_2d, puzzle_3d, puzzle_5d) that wraps the already-established `<Projection as vcs::DocumentDsl>::parse_dsl` + `serde_json::to_string` bridge (same logic puzzle-plugin already uses internally via LazyLock<String>, just not yet wasm-exposed), rebuild each crate's wasm pkg via `bun nx run <pkg>:wasm`, then update the three story files to `?raw`-import the DSL text fixtures and parse them through the rebuilt wasm module instead of importing deleted JSON. This keeps Rust's parse_dsl as the single source of truth instead of duplicating the DSL grammar in TypeScript or committing a stale generated JSON snapshot.

Verify via `bun nx run workspace:build-storybook` completing successfully, then run .storybook/styling.spec.ts and .storybook/os-plugins.spec.ts via Playwright to confirm the whole verification pipeline is unblocked.
summary:
Fixed the three puzzle Storybook story files (2d/3d/5d) that broke when ticket CONVERT-PUZZLE-2D-3D-5D-TO-TYPED-DSL-DERIVE-ENGINE deleted their *.2d.json/*.3d.json/*.5d.json fixtures. Added one small free #[wasm_bindgen] export per crate (puzzle2dParseDslJson/puzzle3dParseDslJson/puzzle5dParseDslJson) wrapping the crates' existing parse_dsl+serde_json::to_string bridge, so Rust's DSL parser stays the single source of truth instead of duplicating the DSL grammar in TypeScript or committing a stale generated JSON snapshot. Updated the three story files to ?raw-import the real .puzzle2d/.puzzle3d/.puzzle5d DSL-text fixtures and parse them via the new wasm exports at story-mount time (module-promise-cached, matching framework/renderer/react/index.tsx's existing createEngineSession pattern), with an async loading state.

While rebuilding puzzle-5d-rs's wasm package, found and fixed a separate pre-existing latent bug: Puzzle5dPrecomputeSession's set_scene/apply_brush_placement_rust/apply_fill_count_rust unconditionally called puzzle_3d::Puzzle3dPrecomputeSession's native/p2-only (_rust-suffixed) methods, which don't exist on that struct's plain-wasm32 (browser, non-p2) impl variant — meaning puzzle_5d's own `wasm-pack build --target web` had apparently never compiled before. Fixed by splitting into two cfg-gated impls mirroring puzzle_3d's own existing split (native/p2 gets the Puzzle3dError-typed _rust methods, plain wasm32 gets JsValue-typed short-named methods).

Also fixed one unrelated stale one-line Storybook alias (.storybook/scopes.ts: @semio-tech/compose-algorithm pointed at compose/dev/algorithm/index.ts, missing the /js/ segment) that was blocking ANY Storybook build (full or scoped) regardless of the puzzle fix.

Verification: all three wasm packages rebuild clean with the new exports confirmed in pkg/*.d.ts. Wrote a standalone verification page (.repo/🎫️/26/07/27/FIX-STORYBOOK-BUILD-BROKEN-BY-PUZZLE-DSL-FIXTURE-MIGRATION/verify-wasm-parse.html) served via plain python http.server (bypassing Vite/Storybook), loaded in a real browser: confirmed zero console errors, both concrete-forest and nakagin-capsule-tower (180-item) fixtures parse to camelCase JSON matching the pre-migration fixture shape exactly and field-for-field matching the three story files' TS types. Full bun nx run workspace:build-storybook now gets past ALL puzzle-related imports with zero puzzle errors (confirmed progressing further than before, 200 modules transformed) before hitting an UNRELATED pre-existing failure in coda/client/ui/desktop/js/renderer.tsx (can't resolve @semio-tech/framework-platform-core) — confirmed via git status this file is independently modified by other concurrent work, not touched by this ticket. A scoped build attempt also hit a second unrelated pre-existing bug in compose/dev/algorithm/js/index.ts's own relative imports. Storybook's interactive dev server additionally crashes on startup (any scope) from an unrelated esbuild/fsevents/addon-vitest native-module bundling issue, reproduced twice. None of these three remaining blockers trace back to the puzzle DSL fixture migration this ticket targeted — full details and reasoning in verification-notes.md. The two Playwright specs (styling.spec.ts, os-plugins.spec.ts) could not be run end-to-end as a result and remain blocked on those unrelated issues.
